definitions.definition: A way of organizing documents into groups based on their main topic or theme.
definitions.example: Like sorting books into different shelves by subject.

definitions.definition: The starting conditions or assumptions used as a reference point.
definitions.example: Setting the starting line before a race.

definitions.definition: Resistance or opposition to an idea or claim.
definitions.example: When someone disagrees with your opinion and argues against it.

definitions.definition: A change that makes something unclear, inaccurate, or misleading.
definitions.example: Looking at your reflection in a funhouse mirror.

definitions.definition: The ability to judge well and tell the difference between things that are similar.
definitions.example: Knowing which advice to follow and which to ignore.

definitions.definition: The act of bringing something back to its original good condition.
definitions.example: Fixing a broken toy so it works like new again.

definitions.definition: Putting something back together after it has been taken apart.
definitions.example: Putting the pieces of a puzzle back together.

definitions.definition: The quality of being logical, consistent, and holding together as a whole.
definitions.example: A story that makes sense from beginning to end.

definitions.definition: The process of combining separate parts into a single, unified system.
definitions.example: Mixing different colors of paint to make a new color.

definitions.definition: Documents that are complete on their own and not part of a larger group.
definitions.example: A single Lego figure that isn't part of a set.

definitions.definition: Items that are related by topic or theme, placed close together.
definitions.example: Putting all books about dinosaurs on the same shelf.
